subject: RFP follow-up: Operational on-call model, escalation gates & communication templates
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@apexbank.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@apexbank.com
Date: 2026-11-28T07:45:00-08:00
Subject: ApexBank RFP 1: ops/on-call clarifications

Hi Michael / Marissa,

Thanks for the materials submitted with the RFP. Our SOC and procurement teams have a couple of targeted questions so we can document controls for internal reviewers: 

1) On-call model: for Enterprise tier please provide the typical rotation length (weeks), number of engineers per rotation, and whether you maintain a geographically separated secondary. Is there a documented handover process?
2) Escalation gates: what automated triggers move an incident from TAM -> engineering -> incident commander? Are those triggers auditable and do they generate a timestamped audit entry?
3) Communications: please share a short example update for a Sev1 at T+30 and a post-incident report template.

We attached the RFP spreadsheet section 5 with the questions highlighted. Can you send the examples and a redacted audit log sample before our tabletop? Procurement also needs to confirm termination windows in the SOW.

Regards,
Elena Ruiz
Director, Cloud Security Programs
ApexBank

Attachment: APX_RFP_section5_ops.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: michael_grant@redwood.com <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@apexbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: ApexBank RFP !: ops/on-call clarifications

Elena 5 thanks for the clear ask. Quick summary and I'm attaching a short on-call model doc and a sample T+30 update. We'll join the tabletop to walk through the flow.

On-call model (Enterprise recommended):
- Rotation cadence: 2-week rotations for primary engineers (typical); 2-person primary rotation + 1 geographically separated backup.
- Coverage: 24x7 L2 monitoring + on-call TAM for customer-facing coordination. Primary engineering rotates weekly for very large accounts on request.
- Handover: standardized handover template (shift start/stop, open incidents, key actions) stored in the account runbook; each handover generates an audit entry.

Escalation gates / automation:
- Triggers: severity from monitoring alerts, manual TAM elevation, SLA breach (X minutes without ack).
- Automation: integration with pager/alerting system -> automatic page and Slack bridge for Sev1. All escalations create timestamped audit log entries (who, when, trigger, actions).

Communications (examples attached):
- T+30 Sev1 update: 1) brief impact statement; 2) mitigation steps underway; 3) ETA for next update; 4) who is leading.
- Post-incident: RCA template with timeline, root cause, mitigation, and long-term remediation plan (72-hour target for Sev1 draft).

Procurement note: we can support a 60-day termination for pilot agreements; commercial will confirm final SOW language.

I'll bring Neha and Karthik onto the tabletop to review the audit log/redaction approach and encryption details. Proposed tabletop: 2026-12-09 09:00 PT (30 min).

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Oncall_Model.pdf, Sev1_Incident_Update_Template.txt

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@apexbank.com>
Cc: michael_grant@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T11:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: ApexBank RFP !: ops/on-call clarifications

Elena 5 following up with a TAM perspective and the onboarding checklist attached. A few operational notes for your SOC review: 

- TAM responsibilities: customer communication, initial triage coordination, and ensuring runbook steps are followed; TAMs will not override engineering incident triage decisions but will coordinate status updates and stakeholder bridging.
- Escalation ownership: for Sev1 the on-call TAM triggers the automated escalation and remains primary contact until engineering declares mitigation or hands to Incident Commander.
- Auditability: we keep a redacted audit log for each escalation step (timestamp, actor, note). We can provide a sanitized sample for your reviewers.

If ApexBank prefers a tabletop focused on automation triggers, let us know and we'll structure the session accordingly.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment: TAM_Onboarding_Checklist.xlsx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: ApexBank RFP !: ops/on-call clarifications

Elena 5 short note from the solutions/ops side:

- Audit logs: each escalation step is stored with a UUID, actor, and timestamp. We can provide a redacted CSV sample that strips PII but preserves timing/step fidelity.
- KMS/integration: runbooks reference customer KMS key IDs for log encryption at rest; we also support cross-account key wrapping patterns for on-prem deployments.
- Evidence for compliance: we can produce a redacted timeline export and a sample Slack bridge transcript (sanitized) if SOC wants to validate comms flow.

Happy to walk through specifics during the tabletop.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
